The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (Tan); MemoraX AI (Gu, Li, Hu, He, Li, Hao); corresponding author e-mail at tju.edu.cn

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Evaluates — benchmark EngramBench for skill-evolution harnesses (30 learning tasks, 13 transfer tasks, two-phase frozen protocol, CCPF metric); evaluation of static skill banks against a No Skills baseline with two ablations on 4 transfer tasks
fields.why: Main nature (benchmark = proposes an evaluation method) is clear from the contributions (p. 3-4). The secondary is a judgement: four configurations are run against each other (Compares) but all are variants of one skill-bank approach vs none (Evaluates)

fields.v: Static skill banks (procedural memory, SKILL.md) distilled from learning-phase trajectories by a two-stage pipeline (local distillation into 368 raw skill packages, then global compression with DeepSeek V4 Pro at temperature 0); configurations S-Full-20, S-Ablated-20 (from history with 69.66% of text removed), Coreless-3 (3 basic interface skills). Pipeline not named; no version

Per task: definitive README contract (immutable requirements), frozen execution plan, user scenario, deterministic scaffold with request/response contracts and public interface checker; skill bank (SKILL.md) frozen with SHA-256 manifest

Phase 1: learning tasks run, trajectories distilled into skill bank, bank frozen. Phase 2: transfer task with README, clean scaffold and frozen bank; multi-turn development driven by simulated user against frozen plan; iterate against public interface checker; commit frozen; hidden evaluation in separate container
None during runs (LLM-simulated user replaces human); tasks and distilled skills 'verified through human-expert baseline executions'; manual trajectory auditing mentioned
Single artefact varied (skill bank); README contract and frozen plan held fixed in all configurations

Not classifiable — authors do not use SDD terms; tasks are 'requirement-driven' from a 'definitive README contract' and a 'frozen execution plan' (closest to spec-first, reviewer's reading); the varied artefact is a skill bank, not a specification
fields.why: The README contract and frozen plan are fixed inputs, not the object studied (the skill bank is); 'not classifiable' vs 'spec-first' is a judgement for the author

Criterion: micro-average CCPF on 4 transfer tasks, 3 trials each (12 runs per configuration); coding agent GPT-5.5 Medium (agent harness not named), simulated user DeepSeek V4 Pro. - No Skills (baseline) + GPT-5.5 Medium: CCPF 46.63% (MeterSettle 76.42, FlagFoundry 46.34, EscrowGuard 18.52, CapacityLease 47.83); 50.0M tokens, 3.21M non-cached input, 27.0 turns, 189.00 min per run. Quality partly (under half of hidden cases passed); cost does not work (about 3 h and 50M tokens per run). - S-Full-20 + GPT-5.5 Medium: CCPF 51.25% (80.49 / 47.15 / 33.33 / 46.38); 40.2M tokens, 0.61M non-cached, 26.5 turns, 84.46 min. Quality partly (about half of hidden cases; uneven across tasks); cost partly (84 min, 40M tokens per run). - S-Ablated-20 (ablation) + GPT-5.5 Medium: CCPF 52.60%, 91.74 min. Quality partly; cost partly. - Coreless-3 (ablation, exploratory, designed after seeing results) + GPT-5.5 Medium: CCPF 48.36%, >=190.87 min; 26 compactions, 699,961 reasoning tokens (totals over 12 runs). Quality partly; cost does not work. Per-task CCPF only reported for No Skills and S-Full-20; tokens per run only for No Skills and S-Full-20
fields.why: All numbers checked against Tables 2-5 (p. 11-12). Verdict levels are a judgement: e.g. about 85-90 min and 40M tokens per run for S-Full-20 / S-Ablated-20 could be read as 'partly' or 'does not work', and CCPF around 50% as 'partly' or 'does not work'

fields.v: Tasks: 4 of 13 transfer tasks. Configurations: No Skills, S-Full-20, S-Ablated-20, Coreless-3. Baseline: No Skills. Held constant: coding model (GPT-5.5 Medium), simulated user (DeepSeek V4 Pro thinking/high), README, frozen plan, scenario, learning trajectories, Docker sandbox. Acceptance: hidden evaluators. Repetitions: 3 trials per configuration-task pair (48 trajectories). Human intervention: none in runs. S-Full-20 bank selected by qualitative coverage, not transfer scores

S-Full-20 vs No Skills: CCPF +4.62 pp (51.25 vs 46.63; EscrowGuard +14.81, CapacityLease -1.45); tokens -19.66%, non-cached input -80.91%, turns -1.85%, coding time -55.3% (189.00 -> 84.46 min). S-Ablated-20 highest CCPF (52.60%), +8.6% time vs S-Full-20. Coreless-3 CCPF 48.36%, time above baseline; tool invocations +68.97% and reasoning tokens +131.76% vs S-Full-20. Patch invocations -29.8% with S-Full-20. No significance tests or variance reported

Distinguished configurations mainly on time and token cost; correctness differences small and uneven with 3 trials per cell and no statistics. Limitations stated: computational scale (up to 66M tokens per run, manual auditing) restricts study to 48 runs on 4 tasks; only frozen skill banks (no dynamic retrieval); single coding model; evaluator isolation to be hardened; Coreless-3 exploratory

Static skill banks do not bypass the 'last mile' of exact implementation (bounded by base model) but act as an 'execution compass', cutting coding time by over 55%; history volume matters less than abstracted knowledge. Future: scale audit to all 13 tasks, test open-weight models, dynamic memory retrieval, stricter air-gapped evaluator isolation
